title: Equities update - November 23rd 2026
summary: Blockchain equities fell 9.5% in Week 47 as the VIX topped 40 and a broad sell-off hit risk assets. Read our weekly update on Strategy, Circle and tokenised deposits.
body_markdown:
Week 47 saw US equity volatility reach a new high for the year, with the VIX briefly trading above 40 on Friday. The sell-off pushed the Nasdaq Composite to a (2.7%) year-to-date loss and left the S&P 500 and Dow close to flat, up 0.9% and 0.2%, respectively. This came despite strong Nvidia earnings and management raising its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to around 75%. Anthropic also raised a record US$81.3bn in its IPO and closed its first day 17% above the offer price. The debut showed that investors would still commit capital to select AI names, although an offering of that size may also have drawn some buying power away from existing holdings. For BLOCK’s miners moving into AI, Nvidia’s potential US$32bn of neocloud commitments underscored the distinction between demand and financing with operators still needing to fund construction and bring capacity online before Nvidia takes delivery. Elsewhere on the corporate side, Circle’s agreement with DBS, Standard Chartered’s expansion of tokenised deposits and Citi and Circle’s work with the World Bank Group point to a different source of growth. If institutions use these services routinely to move and hold cash, they could broaden the Index’s earnings drivers beyond crypto prices and trading volumes.


## Week 47 Key Developments in Blockchain Equities:


-


Index Performance:


The Index fell (9.5%) over the week, while Bitcoin declined approximately (10.2%), as a broad sell-off swept across risk assets. The October FOMC minutes, released on Wednesday, reinforced the Fed’s tightening bias; almost all participants expected further rate increases to be appropriate, and a couple were open to a hike of more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if inflation came in hotter than expected. Strong Nvidia results and a successful debut for Anthropic’s record-setting IPO failed to stem the AI sell-off, with growth equities approaching their April lows. The US Dollar Index (DXY) rose to 103.5 as investors cut risk and favoured cash, adding to the pressure on growth stocks and digital assets.


-


Block Index Key Movers:


7-day top performers:


GMO Internet (+5.0%), Sony (+1.9%), Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Holdings (+1.5%).


7-day worst performers:


Bitdeer (−44.4%), IREN (−26.0%), Strategy (−24.7%).


-


Asia’s banks are bringing tokenised assets into corporate treasury - Circle


and


DBS


announced on that eligible institutions can mint and redeem USDC through DBS, with near-real-time settlement between US dollars and USDC around the clock. Meanwhile,


Standard Chartered


is addressing a related need through tokenised commercial bank deposits, enabling eligible clients to move cash between Singapore and Hong Kong in near real time, including between entities within the same group. The Monetary Authority of Singapore also demonstrated how tokenised money can settle securities, using wholesale central bank digital currency to settle a S$100m four-week bill issue on its test network. For BLOCK, which holds both Circle and Standard Chartered, the longer-term opportunity is to gain exposure to routine corporate cash management and settlement, diversifying the Index’s earnings drivers beyond crypto prices and trading volumes. For Circle, the benefit would come from institutions holding USDC as working cash between transactions, supporting reserve income after distribution costs. For Standard Chartered, faster transfers could help retain operating deposits and win more FX, payments and custody business. Sustained USDC balances, repeat corporate usage and evidence of deposit retention or incremental fees will show whether these services are translating into earnings.


-


Earnings Recap – Key Holdings:


-


Bullish


– Mixed


### Other news - Index constituents:


-


Coinbase


published a proposed standard with Broadridge to deliver shareholder communications to wallets holding tokenised shares. The companies submitted it as an Ethereum Improvement Proposal, and Broadridge announced a data oracle for issuer events. The aim is to help investors receive the documents they need to exercise their rights wherever they hold the shares. Separately, on 17 November, Coinbase expanded its Morpho-powered USDC borrowing product to eligible New York customers, who can take out variable-rate loans against BTC, ETH or SOL.


-


Strategy Inc


disclosed on 16 November that it bought 485 BTC for US$33.4m, taking holdings to 850,849 BTC, and repurchased US$228.1m of STRC. Of US$244.7m raised through common equity, US206.3m went to preferred repurchases. The company ended 15 November with a US4.75bn reserve for dividends and interest and US$151.2m in separate USD cash.


-


Metaplanet


published materials on 19 November for a shareholder vote on 18 December. It proposes transferring about ¥55.6bn from stated capital and capital reserves to other capital surplus, increasing the amount legally available for future class-share dividends and buybacks. The change would give management more flexibility over how it finances the Bitcoin treasury and returns capital to shareholders.


-


Citi


and


Circle


announced on 17 November that they would work with the W


orld Bank Group


to explore using USDC to disburse development funds. The initiative builds on FundsChain, which already tracks spending across more than 350 projects in 96 countries. The opportunity is to connect that visibility with the movement of money itself, potentially making disbursements faster and easier to reconcile.


### Other news – Non - Index constituents:


-


Invesco and Superstate


launched the


Invesco Stablecoin Reserves Onchain Fund


on 17 November, giving stablecoin issuers a tokenised vehicle for holding short-dated US Treasuries and other eligible reserve assets. This opens a route for asset managers to earn fees from stablecoin growth by managing the assets backing the tokens.


-


DBS and JPMorgan


launched a service on 16 November that lets institutions move tokenised US dollar deposits between the US and Singapore around the clock, with


Ant International


as the first client. This adds a useful distinction to the main thematic: corporate treasurers can move liquidity between two banks’ tokenised deposit networks. If more banks connect, that could reduce the need to pre-fund accounts in multiple markets


-


HSBC


expanded its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin


RedCoin


into retail wealth management on 19 November, allowing customers to subscribe to a tokenised money market fund from


HK$100


. This gives customers a reason to use the stablecoin beyond payments and gives HSBC another way to distribute its own funds. Repeat subscriptions would show whether the integration attracts new balances.


-


Nihon Chokuhan


began trialling


JPYC


payments on its Japanese e-commerce site on 19 November. Customers use MetaMask to pay in yen stablecoins without bearing the network fee. It’s a practical test of stablecoins in ordinary retail checkout, although the need for a separate wallet and payment link leaves some friction for shoppers.
